generation.explanation: A secant line cuts through two points on a curve: a fixed point P at x = a and a nearby point Q at x = a + h. As h shrinks toward zero, Q slides toward P and the secant rotates into a limiting position—the tangent line. The slope of that tangent is the derivative f'(a), the instantaneous rate of change at a.
